clue.text: No law breaker, but he keeps PC busy

definitions.text: No law breaker, but he keeps PC busy

parts.words: No law breaker, but he keeps PC busy
parts.note: PC suggests a police constable chasing a criminal, but here it is a personal computer kept busy by someone glued to the screen and clicking away

explanation.surface: A man who keeps the local police officer busy without actually being a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: PC wants to be the police constable, which 'law breaker' encourages; it is the personal computer. The answer is modelled on 'couch potato', with the computer's pointing device in place of the sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a person who spends long idle hours at a computer, as a couch potato does in front of television.

clue.text: Many and various pipes in the engine

definitions.meaning: numerous and of many kinds, an old sense
the branched pipe carrying gases to or from an engine's cylinders

explanation.definitionFit: The word means of many kinds, and names the branched pipe assembly on an engine.

clue.text: Not meant. Not Neglected

definitions.meaning: not intended, with the archaic tend meaning intend

explanation.surface: Something unintentional that has also been left uncared for.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as not intended it means unplanned; ordinarily it means left without care or attention.

clue.text: Reflective poem set for instance in cathedral city

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation goes inside the city name

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
eg, exempli gratia, means for instance

explanation.surface: A thoughtful poem set in a city with a cathedral, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England; EG goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mournful, meditative poem, typically a lament for the dead.

clue.text: In sum, two ducks, terrible -not looking good

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters are in a dreadful mess and must be rearranged

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like the letter O, so two ducks give two Os

explanation.surface: Adding it up, two zero scores is a terrible omen.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nought in cricket, so two ducks are OO; 'terrible' rearranges them with IN SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Threatening, suggesting that something bad is about to happen.

clue.text: No paintings without skill!

explanation.surface: A gallery with no pictures, run by people with no talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Split, it describes having no art; as one word it means guileless, without craft.

clue.text: Possibly phone round work Everyone welcome

indicators.note: possibly suggests the word phone could be arranged in another way

parts.note: O is the shape of something round
use means to work or employ

explanation.surface: A host perhaps phoning round to say all are invited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges PHONE to OPENH, followed by O and USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A party or event at which hospitality is offered to all comers.

clue.text: A quiet wood

parts.note: sh is the instruction to be quiet

explanation.surface: A peaceful stretch of woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: The timber of a common hardwood tree, used for tool handles and bats.

clue.text: Canvas sheet coming to light, top missing

indicators.note: top missing means the first letter, at the top of a down entry, is removed

parts.note: dawning means becoming clear or coming to light

explanation.surface: A canvas sheet being revealed with its top part gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top missing' removes the D from DAWNING.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet of canvas stretched over a frame to shelter a window or doorway from sun or rain.

clue.text: Slip in class?

parts.note: a slip made by a pupil in class, a blunder so glaring that it gets laughed at

explanation.surface: A student making a mistake during a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A glaring blunder, especially a schoolchild's comic error.

clue.text: A fool regarding the gunpowder constituent

parts.note: a nit is a foolish person, British slang
re means regarding or concerning, as in a business letter

explanation.surface: Someone foolish asking questions about what goes into gunpowder.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate, also called saltpetre, is the oxidising ingredient of black powder.

clue.text: Who in Kent surprisingly becomes aware?

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of the words before it turn up in an unexpected arrangement

explanation.surface: A question about which resident of the English county of Kent has suddenly woken up to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges the nine letters of WHO IN KENT. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone informed about a matter, with inside information, is said to be aware of it.

clue.text: Spooner's rabbit, mobile, is part of the joint

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words for rabbit and mobile are exchanged

parts.note: a bunny is a child's word for a rabbit
a phone, as in a mobile phone

explanation.surface: A Spoonerism about a rabbit and a mobile somehow linked to a joint of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of BUNNY and PHONE gives FUNNY and BONE; the PH sound counts as F.
explanation.definitionFit: The spot at the back of the elbow where a nerve lies close to the skin, so knocking it tingles.

clue.text: All depends on it, nothing excepted (only in part)

indicators.note: only in part tells you just a portion of the words in front of it is used, the letters running across the word break

explanation.surface: A grand claim that everything rests on one thing, with nothing left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'nothing' into the start of 'excepted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially everything turns on a pivot: we say a result hinges on something.

clue.text: Left cheese perhaps to the spongers

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word cheese might be rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: Someone has left out cheese for freeloaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is the anagram signal; 'Left' gives its usual one-letter abbreviation at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodsucking worms give their name to people who live off others without giving anything back.

clue.text: Judges will follow this group

parts.note: Judges is the seventh book of the Bible, so it comes after the group made of the first six books

explanation.surface: A panel of judges who will go along with what a certain group decides.
explanation.walkthrough: Judges looks like officials of a court; it is the Old Testament book that comes after the first six books.
explanation.definitionFit: The first six books of the Old Testament, Genesis to Joshua, treated as one collection.

clue.text: KO crazy back

indicators.note: back says the word for crazy is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: nuts is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A knockout leaves someone dazed and wandering back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NUTS round to give the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockout blow leaves a boxer dazed and senseless, as does any heavy shock.

clue.text: Reliable supporter's last time to become excited about conflict

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the word for conflict
to become excited suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A loyal backer whose final hour is spent getting worked up over a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become excited' gives the anagram (STALT) and 'about' puts it round the conflict. The 's of supporter's stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal, dependable member or backer of a team or party.

clue.text: Lush? Quite a soak needed

definitions.meaning: a lush is slang for a heavy drinker
a soak is a habitual drinker

explanation.surface: A drink-sodden person who needs a long soak in the bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual heavy drinker, called both a lush and a soak in slang.

clue.text: Fixed reference line for team in a second

indicators.note: in says the team goes inside the other two pieces

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football side

explanation.surface: A team trying to fix its position in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a side in cricket or football; it sits inside A and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight line against which positions are measured, as on a graph, or about which something rotates.

clue.text: Arrange canvas and start on course

parts.note: to set something is to arrange it
a sail is made of canvas

explanation.surface: Sailors arranging the canvas and beginning their voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin a voyage, to leave port.

clue.text: The rules being broken without universal cover

indicators.note: without says a letter is dropped from the rearranged phrase
rules being broken suggests the letters of the phrase are scrambled

parts.note: U is the film-classification letter for universal, suitable for all

explanation.surface: Rules are being flouted without any general protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being broken' scrambles THE RULES; 'without' removes U, leaving the seven letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuge or roof that protects people from the weather or danger.

clue.text: One out at night not giving a hoot

definitions.text: One out at night not giving a hoot

parts.words: One out at night not giving a hoot
parts.note: a night bird that does not hoot like most of its kind but shrieks instead; not giving a hoot also means not caring

explanation.surface: A carefree night-owl who doesn't care at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not giving a hoot' looks like not caring; it means the bird makes a shrieking call rather than a hoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A night bird named for its harsh shrieking call rather than a hoot.

clue.text: Endlessly awkward from the pampas

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Endlessly awkward from the pampas' (6): GAUCHE endlessly gives only GAUCH; the piece supplying the final O is missing from the clue as held, and no search found the full text.

clue.text: Force a rewrite of poem in class

indicators.note: in says the reworked poem goes inside the class abbreviation

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class

indicators.note: a rewrite of tells you poem is written out again in a different order

explanation.surface: Pupils made to rewrite a poem in class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rewrite of' gives the anagram (OMPE), and 'in' places it inside the class abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige or coerce someone to do something.

clue.text: A top space up the mast

parts.note: a loft is the space at the top of a house, under the roof

explanation.surface: A sailor's spare room at the very top of the mast.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhead, high up in the rigging of a ship.

clue.text: Man in train rigged in waterproof sheet

indicators.note: in says the man's name goes into the middle of the rearranged word
rigged suggests train is fixed into a different arrangement

parts.note: Paul is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone stuck on a train that has been rigged with waterproofing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rigged' gives the anagram (TARIN), and the man's name goes in after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy tarred or plastic canvas used to cover things against rain.

clue.text: Computer storage in body for a bouquet

indicators.note: in says the storage abbreviation goes inside the body

parts.note: the AA, Automobile Association, is a motoring body
ROM is read-only memory, computer storage

explanation.surface: Computer memory inside a body, standing in for a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA, the Automobile Association, is a British motoring organisation, counted as a body.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its smell, a pleasant fragrance.

clue.text: A minor case in the medical world could be

definitions.text: A minor case in the medical world could be

parts.words: A minor case in the medical world could be
parts.note: a minor case suggests an unimportant patient, but it is a small container for a dose of medicine, and something sealed in one is described by this word

explanation.surface: A doctor speculating about a mild illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests a patient; it is a small casing round a medicine dose, and the answer means enclosed in such a casing.
explanation.definitionFit: Enclosed in a small soluble shell, as medicines are packed in pills.

clue.text: Ring master with home originally a city in US

parts.note: O is the shape of a ring
MA, Master of Arts, is a master's degree

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word home

explanation.surface: A circus ringmaster going back to his home town in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring master' reads as the circus ringmaster but splits into O and MA, a Master of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city in the state of Nebraska.

clue.text: See 20
A father held to be disorderly showing little enthusiasm

indicators.note: disorderly suggests the letters of the phrase are in a jumbled state

explanation.surface: A father who is detained for disorderly conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be disorderly' rearranges all eleven letters of A FATHER HELD.
explanation.definitionFit: Done without real commitment or spirit, lacking zeal.
